import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Denominators of $\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{k 2^k}$

$a(n)$ is the denominator of the sum
$$\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{i} \binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$$

*References:*
- [A175386](https://oeis.org/A175386)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA175386


/--
$a(n)$ is the denominator of the sum
$$\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{i} \binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.sum (Finset.Icc 1 n) fun i : ℕ =>
    -- The upper index is $2n - i - 1$, which is equivalent to
    -- $2n - (i+1)$ in $\mathbb{N}$ for $i \le n$.
    -- The lower index $i-1$ is standard subtraction in $\mathbb{N}$.
    let num : ℕ := Nat.choose (2 * n - (i + 1)) (i - 1)
    (num : ℚ) / (i : ℚ)
  ).den



@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 6 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 4 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by native_decide


/--
We conjecture that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{i} \binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$ is not an integer for $n > 1$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/175386.wip.lean#L304"]
theorem a_ne_one (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : a n ≠ 1 := by
    sorry

end OeisA175386

findings.description: The module heading at line 20 says “Denominators of ∑_{k=1}^n 1/(k 2^k)”, which is a different sequence from both OEIS A175386 and the correctly implemented definition `OeisA175386.a`. For example, at n = 1 the heading's sum has denominator 2, whereas `a 1 = 1`. The definition, its docstring, and the theorem are mathematically correct; only the heading is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A175386, %N: “a(n) = denominator of Sum_{i=1..n} (1/i)*C(2n-i-1,i-1).” Read through the OEIS data mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A175/A175386.seq.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the module heading with “Denominators of $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{i}\binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$”. No Lean declaration needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The source asserts that the binomial sum is not an integer for n > 1; Lean asserts that its reduced rational denominator is not 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every q : ℚ, q.den = 1 if and only if there exists z : ℤ with (z : ℚ) = q: one direction uses q.num as the witness, and integer casts have denominator 1 for the converse. Negating gives the required equivalence. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, `Review.a_eq_source_den` identifies `a` with the denominator of the literal source formula, and `Review.faithful_statement` proves the equivalence under the full quantification ∀ n : ℕ, 1 < n → …. Its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

review.notes: All seven declarations were checked. The definition agrees with all 71 listed OEIS terms, including the five test lemmas. The empty case gives a 0 = 1 and the excluded case gives a 1 = 1. Lean also verifies that every summation index satisfies i ≥ 1 and that both binomial indices are valid, so neither division by zero nor truncated subtraction changes the intended sum. OEIS explicitly records the conjecture as proved by an autonomous AI agent in its May 25, 2026 comment, consistent with `research solved`. The published primary proof has the identical definition and target statement and contains no sorry or custom axiom declarations. Recompiling that older proof after substituting the current import path encountered Lean/Mathlib compatibility errors; I therefore do not claim independent kernel revalidation of the external proof. This does not affect statement faithfulness or establish a status issue. The checkout was not edited.
